rows.description: A teenager uses and decodes references to shows, songs or slang that signal group membership. Outsiders may miss or misread them, and meanings change quickly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager hints "It is getting late" to suggest leaving or implies displeasure without saying it. Hints save face but are often missed, so clear requests avoid confusion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager learns that some remarks carry a suggestive or hurtful second meaning. Recognising these means noticing discomfort, the right to say "that is not okay" and telling a trusted adult if it continues.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager may question rituals, adapt them or find new meaning, sometimes causing tension with family. Respectful questions can coexist with participation, and pressure from either side rarely helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Reverence and respect in shared spaces [Expressing]
rows.description: A teenager shows respect by removing shoes, covering the head, standing or being quiet in a temple, mosque, church or gurdwara. Practices differ, and a visitor can watch others or politely ask.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Hand orientation and palm direction in signs [Interpreting]
rows.description: In signed languages, the direction the palm faces and where the hand points can change a sign's meaning, like a vowel changes a word. Hearing learners must respect this grammar, not treat signs as loose gestures.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A learner watches for hand shape, movement, space and facial grammar to follow meaning, and asks for repetition instead of guessing. Signed languages vary by country and region; there is no single universal sign language.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A deaf or hard-of-hearing teenager may take pride in signing and Deaf culture, while others use spoken language or both. Language choice is personal, and signed languages are valid, complete languages.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager writes essays with a thesis, evidence and counterargument to persuade or explain. Tone in writing must be carried by word choice, since no face or voice supports it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Personal writing and diaries as private space [Regulating]
rows.description: A teenager uses a journal or notes to sort out feelings and identity. Privacy matters, and writing something down does not mean acting on it; worries about safety should be shared with a trusted adult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
